html:
Mount Vesuvius is the volcano on the Bay of Naples in southern Italy, the only active volcano on the European mainland and one of the most dangerous in the world, with some three million people living around it.

The Romans did not know it was a volcano. Its slopes were rich farmland covered in vineyards. In 73 BCE Spartacus and his fellow gladiators camped on its top at the start of their slave revolt, and escaped a Roman siege by climbing down ropes of vines. An earthquake in 62 CE damaged Pompeii, but no one linked it to the mountain.

In 79 CE it erupted and buried Pompeii, Herculaneum and other towns under ash and burning flows of gas and rock. Pliny the Elder, author of the Natural History, died after sailing across the bay to help; his nephew, Pliny the Younger, described the eruption in two letters, and such eruptions are still called Plinian.

It has erupted many times since. The eruption of 1631 killed thousands, and the last, in 1944, destroyed Allied planes on a nearby airfield during World War II.
sum: Mount Vesuvius is the volcano on the Bay of Naples in southern Italy, the only active volcano on the European mainland and one of the most dangerous in the world, with some three million people living around it.
